semantic_findings: 0x00b3d3d0 is a borrowed global-slot accessor: it performs exactly one read and returns the loaded word, with no AddRef, no store, and no lifetime participation of its own.

Both cited callers feed the returned word straight into ECX as a receiver (0x0103ca40, 0x01039730), and the pack's derived `return` field classifies it as `pointer_like` at INFERRED confidence. Both are caller-side use; the body itself proves a four-byte load and nothing about what the word denotes, so no pointee type is asserted.

The calling convention is deliberately left unnamed. With zero parameters, no register read and a bare RET, the body is byte-identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall; the only discriminating fact (`callee pops zero bytes`) is equally true of __cdecl and of zero-parameter __stdcall. The macro PKG_00B3D3D0_CALL is present, named and carries no convention token.

No manager, class or SDK identity is claimed for 0x0167eb20. docs/analysis/simulator-root-closure.md characterizes the sibling accessors 0x00b3d2a0/0x00b3d300/0x00b3d3a0/0x00b3d400 over slots 0x0167eae0/0x0167eae4/0x0167eb0c/0x0167eb60 and never mentions 0x0167eb20 or 0x00b3d3d0, so nothing was imported from it; sibling workers' staging packages were not read as evidence.

The immediate neighbour 0x00b3d3e0 is the same six-byte shape over 0x0167eb24. Recorded as context only: a neighbour's operand is not evidence about this body's return type, receiver or global, and no struct layout or aliasing is claimed for the surrounding .data words.
summary: Six-byte, two-instruction Simulator-family root accessor: MOV EAX,[0x0167eb20]; RET. Reads one global dword from the loader-zeroed tail of .data and returns all four bytes in EAX. Zero parameters, no register read (no receiver), bare RET so zero callee cleanup, zero memory stores. Calling convention is left unnamed because the listing is byte-identical under all four x86-32 conventions.
